summary: A tight, fast-playing cube-rail auction game where players bid on shares, build track, and time dividend calls to maximize their own stock value while starving rivals of income; games run under an hour but every auction and build decision is loaded with opportunity cost. It's considered one of the best entry points into the Winsome/18xx-style stock-and-rail genre because of its short length and clean rules.
praised: Short playtime relative to the depth of decisions
Tense, meaningful share auctions where price-setting matters as much as buying
Good gateway into 18xx-style stock/rail mechanics without the complexity
High replayability from variable company performance each game
criticised: Can feel swingy or luck-influenced by which companies randomly draw good routes
Runaway leader potential if one player dominates early share/track decisions
Thin theme, essentially an abstract economic puzzle
Some feel it's overshadowed by other titles in the same Winsome/Iron Rail lineage

scoring.why: The winner is whoever ends with the highest combined cash and stock value, driven mainly by smart auction timing and dividend calls
